Payroll employment up 303,000 in March 2024
-------------------------------------------

April 11, 2024

Total nonfarm payroll employment rose by 303,000 to 158.1 million in March 2024, higher than the average monthly gain of 231,000 over the prior 12 months. Health care added the most jobs with an increase of 72,000 in March. Over the past 12 months, the industry averaged a gain of 60,000 jobs per month.

*   Chart Image
*   Chart Data

### Employment levels by industry, March 2014 to March 2024

Line chart with 21 lines.

The chart has 1 X axis displaying categories. 

The chart has 1 Y axis displaying Millions. Data ranges from 6038000 to 158133000.

End of interactive chart.

| Jan 2024 | 16,813,000 | 5,874,000 | 23,136,000 | 2,974,000 | 5,420,000 | 14,742,000 |
| Feb 2024 | 16,856,000 | 5,885,000 | 23,199,000 | 2,984,000 | 5,431,000 | 14,784,000 |
| Mar 2024 | 16,905,000 | 5,901,000 | 23,270,000 | 2,993,000 | 5,444,000 | 14,833,000 |
| Note: Data are seasonally adjusted. |

Employment in government increased by 71,000 from February 2024 to March 2024, higher than the average monthly gain of 54,000 over the prior 12 months. Employment increased in local government (+49,000) and federal government (+9,000) in March. Leisure and hospitality employment trended up in March 2024 (+49,000) and has returned to its pre-pandemic February 2020 level. Over the prior 12 months, job growth in the industry averaged 37,000 per month. Construction employment was up 39,000 over the month, about double the average monthly gain of 19,000 over the prior 12 months.

Employment in the other services (+16,000) and social assistance (+9,000) industries continued to trend upward in March. Little or no employment change was seen over the month in other major industries, including retail trade; mining, quarrying, and oil and gas extraction; manufacturing; wholesale trade; transportation and warehousing; information; financial activities; and professional and business services.

These data are from the Current Employment Statistics program and are seasonally adjusted. To learn more, see "The Employment Situation — March 2024." Also see more charts of national employment, hours, and earnings data.

 Do you have any suggestions for improvements to the BLS.gov website?  

Submit

Thank you for visiting BLS.gov. You have been randomly chosen to answer a few questions to let us know what we're doing well and where we can improve BLS.gov. The feedback you provide will help us improve your website experience.

This voluntary survey is being collected by the Bureau of Labor Statistics under OMB No. 1225-0088 (Expiration Date: 1/31/2027). We estimate that this survey takes 3 minutes to complete. If you have any comments regarding this estimate, send them to BLS_PRA_Public@bls.gov. You are not required to respond to this collection unless it displays a currently valid OMB control number. Your participation is voluntary, and you have the right to stop at any time.

 This survey is being administered by Touchpoints and resides on a server outside of the BLS Domain. The BLS cannot guarantee the protection of survey responses and advises against the inclusion of sensitive personal information in any response.
